# Hollow duplicates (what the regenerated copy of a carried thing is like)
<!-- When a piece the party already carries regrows in the world after a reset, the
     world's copy is inert (`notes: duplicate; hollow`). Roll 1d10 for its flavour, or
     pick. Also usable for any loop-worn thing the GM wants to make funny. -->

| roll | result |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Looks exactly right, weighs nothing, and tastes, if licked, of absolutely nothing. Its holder has noticed and is pretending not to |
| 2 | A glass bead. The guardian is as fierce about it as ever and will not hear a word against it |
| 3 | The right stone, but painted on: a flat patch of colour on wood, horn or ice that comes off on a thumb |
| 4 | It is there, and it works, for about a minute, and then it is a pebble and the guardian looks at it the way Bramblewick looks at his hooves |
| 5 | A hollow shell; shaken, something rattles inside; opened, it holds a very small paper crown with a goose on it |
| 6 | The copy is where it should be, and the party's real one grows warm and hums at it, as if embarrassed |
| 7 | Missing entirely. The guardian is wearing an empty wire, an empty setting or an empty hand, and insists it is there, and will fight you for it |
| 8 | A perfect copy made of ice, melting; the guardian is trying to keep it cold and failing; sympathy is possible |
| 9 | The copy has the colour but not the virtue, and the guardian's whole routine has gone flat with it: the toast ends on time, the reel drags, the song is only loud. Nobody knows why today feels thin |
| 10 | It is a sausage. Nobody can explain this. The guardian does not want to talk about it |
